subproblem.title: Mass-measure limits of blow-ups of a cone at p are invariant under translations along ℝp
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, all C, C' ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n, ℝ^P := Euclid P), every p ∈ ℝ^P and every sequence λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0: if C is integer multiplicity and a cone (IsConeCurrent C), and the mass measures of the blow-ups blowUp C p λ_j converge to that of C' (MassMeasuresConverge (fun j => blowUp C p λ_j) C'), then for every integer multiplicity representation R' of C' (R' : IMRep univ n with R'.Represents C'), every v ∈ span{p} and every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P: μ'((· + v)^{-1}(A)) = μ'(A), where μ' := R'.measure = mult·H^n⌞carrier.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C C' : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (p : Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (hlams : ∀ j, 0 < lams j), IsIntegerMultiplicity C → IsConeCurrent C → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → MassMeasuresConverge (fun j => blowUp C p (lams j) (hlams j).ne') C' → ∀ R' : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, R'.Represents C' → ∀ v ∈ Submodule.span ℝ {p}, ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R'.measure ((fun x => x + v) ⁻¹' A) = R'.measure A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–5 of the parent proof of `idtp_cone_tangent_cone_planar`, written for an arbitrary degree n. This is the step 'ψ_{βx,1} = lim φ_{x+λ_jβx,λ_j} = ψ for all β ∈ ℝ' in Simon's proof of Theorem A.4 (chapter-A.txt lines 125–131), which uses that φ is a cone (φ_{0,λ} = φ) and which the book calls evident; here it is carried out for the mass measures of the blow-ups of a cone current. Notation: ℝ^P := Euclid P; τ_v(x) := x + v; m_s(x) := s·x; η_j := dilation p λ_j, η_j(x) = λ_j^{-1}(x − p), an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with η_j^{-1}(B) = p + λ_jB; C_c is the set of continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support (the condition tsupport f ⊆ univ in MassMeasuresConverge is automatic).
1. (Representations of the blow-ups.) C is integer multiplicity: fix R : IMRep univ n with R.Represents C and put μ := R.measure. For each j the accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_imrep` (P, n, U := univ, T := C, x := p, λ := λ_j, R) gives R_j : IMRep (η_j '' univ) n with R_j.Represents (blowUp C p λ_j) and R_j.measure(B) = ofReal(λ_j^{-n})·μ(η_j^{-1}(B)) for every Borel B. Put μ_j := R_j.measure and μ' := R'.measure. As η_j is continuous, two measures agreeing on Borel sets are equal, so μ_j = ofReal(λ_j^{-n})·(η_j)_#μ, and hence ∫ g dμ_j = λ_j^{-n} ∫ g(η_j(x)) dμ(x) for every g ∈ C_c (integral against a scalar multiple of a push-forward).
2. (Local finiteness.) For an IMRep R° in univ and compact K, R°.measure(K) = ∫_{carrier ∩ K} mult dH^n < ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult. So μ and μ' are finite on compact sets, and so is μ_j because η_j^{-1}(K) is compact. In particular every g ∈ C_c is integrable for μ, μ_j, μ'. Applying MassMeasuresConverge to the representations (R_j)_j and R' gives (*) ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ' for every f ∈ C_c.
3. (Cone scaling.) Since C is a cone, the accepted `Submission.cone_current_imrep_measure_smul_image` (P, n, C, R) gives μ(m_s(A)) = ofReal(s^n)·μ(A) for s > 0 and Borel A. Since m_{s^{-1}}^{-1}(A) = m_s(A), this says (m_{s^{-1}})_#μ = ofReal(s^n)·μ, hence ∫ h(s^{-1}x) dμ(x) = s^n ∫ h dμ for h ∈ C_c.
4. (Translation identity.) Let t ∈ ℝ, j with s := 1 + λ_jt > 0, λ := λ_j, and f ∈ C_c. Since η_j(x) − tp = λ^{-1}(x − p) − tp = λ^{-1}(x − sp), step 1 gives ∫ f(y − tp) dμ_j(y) = λ^{-n} ∫ f(λ^{-1}(x − sp)) dμ(x). With h(z) := f(s·η_j(z)) ∈ C_c we have h(s^{-1}x) = f(sλ^{-1}(s^{-1}x − p)) = f(λ^{-1}(x − sp)), so by step 3 ∫ f(λ^{-1}(x − sp)) dμ(x) = s^n ∫ f(s·η_j(z)) dμ(z), and by step 1 with g(y) := f(sy), λ^{-n} ∫ f(s·η_j(z)) dμ(z) = ∫ f(sy) dμ_j(y). Therefore (**) ∫ f(y − tp) dμ_j(y) = s^n ∫ f(sy) dμ_j(y).
5. (Moving test functions.) Let (s_j) be real numbers with s_j → 1 and f ∈ C_c; we show ∫ f(s_jy) dμ_j(y) → ∫ f dμ'. Choose R₀ ≥ 0 with tsupport f ⊆ closedBall(0, R₀) and let K := closedBall(0, 2R₀). For j large, s_j ≥ 1/2, and then f(s_jy) ≠ 0 implies ‖s_jy‖ ≤ R₀, so ‖y‖ ≤ 2R₀; thus f_j := f(s_j·) and f vanish off K for large j. f is uniformly continuous, and ‖s_jy − y‖ ≤ 2R₀|s_j − 1| on K, so ε_j := sup_y |f_j(y) − f(y)| → 0 (this is also the accepted `Submission.adr_rescaled_translate_tendstoUniformly` with y := 0 and mus j := s_j^{-1}). Choose g ∈ C_c with 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 and g = 1 on K (Urysohn). Then μ_j(K) ≤ ∫ g dμ_j, and ∫ g dμ_j converges by (*), so M := sup_j ∫ g dμ_j < ∞. Hence, for large j, |∫ f_j dμ_j − ∫ f dμ_j| ≤ ε_j μ_j(K) ≤ ε_jM → 0, and ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ' by (*); so ∫ f_j dμ_j → ∫ f dμ'.
6. (Invariance of integrals.) Fix t ∈ ℝ and f ∈ C_c. Since λ_j → 0, s_j := 1 + λ_jt → 1, so s_j > 0 for all j ≥ some j₀. f_t(y) := f(y − tp) lies in C_c, so ∫ f_t dμ_j → ∫ f_t dμ' by (*). By (**), for j ≥ j₀, ∫ f_t dμ_j = s_j^n ∫ f(s_jy) dμ_j(y), which tends to 1·∫ f dμ' by step 5 and s_j^n → 1. By uniqueness of limits, ∫ f(y − tp) dμ'(y) = ∫ f dμ'.
7. (Invariance of the measure.) Let v ∈ span{p}; then v = tp for some t ∈ ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_singleton). Step 6 with −t gives ∫ f(y + v) dμ'(y) = ∫ f dμ' for every f ∈ C_c, i.e. ∫ f d((τ_v)_#μ') = ∫ f dμ' (τ_v is continuous). Both (τ_v)_#μ' and μ' are finite on compact sets (τ_v^{-1}(K) = K − v is compact), hence locally finite Borel measures on the σ-compact metric space ℝ^P and therefore regular (Mathlib instance Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure). By the uniqueness part of the Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported), (τ_v)_#μ' = μ'. Evaluating at a Borel set A gives μ'(τ_v^{-1}(A)) = μ'(A), i.e. R'.measure((fun x => x + v)^{-1}(A)) = R'.measure(A). ∎
proof_key_steps: Represent the blow-ups by dtc_blowUp_imrep: μ_j = λ_j^{-n}(η_j)_#μ_C; all measures are finite on compacts, and MassMeasuresConverge gives ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ' for f ∈ C_c.
Cone scaling of μ_C (cone_current_imrep_measure_smul_image) gives ∫ f(y − tp) dμ_j(y) = s_j^n ∫ f(s_jy) dμ_j(y) with s_j = 1 + λ_jt.
Uniform convergence f(s_j·) → f on a fixed compact set and the bound sup_j μ_j(K) < ∞ give ∫ f(s_jy) dμ_j(y) → ∫ f dμ'.
Hence ∫ f(y − tp) dμ' = ∫ f dμ' for every f ∈ C_c and t ∈ ℝ.
Riesz uniqueness for regular (locally finite) measures gives (τ_v)_#μ' = μ' for v ∈ span{p}.

audit.reason: The exact universal representation contract matches the prose. The proof constructs blow-up representations, establishes local finiteness, derives the correct s_j^n translation identity, and controls moving test functions using uniform convergence, common compact support and bounded compact masses. Eventual positivity suffices. Translation signs and regular-measure uniqueness are correct. The argument also covers n = 0 and p = 0.

subproblem.title: A cone with L-translation-invariant mass measure has density invariant under w ↦ y + λw (y ∈ L)
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n, ℝ^P := Euclid P), every integer multiplicity representation R of S (R : IMRep univ n, R.Represents S) and every linear subspace L ⊆ ℝ^P: if S is a cone (IsConeCurrent S) and R.measure((· + v)^{-1}(A)) = R.measure(A) for every v ∈ L and every Borel A, then for all y ∈ L, λ > 0, w ∈ ℝ^P and θ ∈ ℝ, HasMassDensity S w θ implies HasMassDensity S (y + λw) θ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (L : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), R.Represents S → IsConeCurrent S → (∀ v ∈ L, ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure ((fun x => x + v) ⁻¹' A) = R.measure A) → ∀ y ∈ L, ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ (w : Euclid P) (θ : ℝ), HasMassDensity S w θ → HasMassDensity S (y + lam • w) θ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof of `idtp_cone_tangent_cone_planar`, for an arbitrary degree n and subspace L. Notation: ℝ^P := Euclid P, B_ρ(x) the open ball, ω_n := unitBallVolume n, and r_x(ρ) := M_{B_ρ(x)}(S)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) ∈ [0, ∞] the density ratio, so HasMassDensity S x θ means 0 ≤ θ and r_x(ρ) → ofReal θ as ρ → 0+.
1. (Mass is the measure.) By the accepted `Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure` (a) with U := univ (open), S.massOn W = R.measure W for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P.
2. (Cone scaling.) By the accepted `Submission.cone_current_imrep_measure_smul_image` (P, n, S, R), R.measure((λ•·) '' A) = ofReal(λ^n)·R.measure(A) for λ > 0 and Borel A.
3. Fix y ∈ L, λ > 0, w ∈ ℝ^P and θ with HasMassDensity S w θ, and let ρ > 0. (a) B_ρ(y + λw) = (fun x => x + (−y))^{-1}(B_ρ(λw)), because ‖x − (y + λw)‖ = ‖(x + (−y)) − λw‖; since −y ∈ L and balls are Borel, the hypothesis gives R.measure(B_ρ(y + λw)) = R.measure(B_ρ(λw)). (b) B_ρ(λw) = (λ•·) '' B_{ρ/λ}(w): if ‖z − w‖ < ρ/λ then ‖λz − λw‖ = λ‖z − w‖ < ρ, and conversely z' ∈ B_ρ(λw) equals λ(λ^{-1}z') with ‖λ^{-1}z' − w‖ = λ^{-1}‖z' − λw‖ < ρ/λ. By step 2, R.measure(B_ρ(λw)) = ofReal(λ^n)·R.measure(B_{ρ/λ}(w)). (c) With step 1: M_{B_ρ(y+λw)}(S) = ofReal(λ^n)·M_{B_{ρ/λ}(w)}(S).
4. (Ratios.) For ρ > 0, ρ^n = λ^n(ρ/λ)^n with both factors ≥ 0, so ofReal(ρ^n) = ofReal(λ^n)·ofReal((ρ/λ)^n), and c := ofReal(λ^n) satisfies 0 < c < ∞. By step 3(c), r_{y+λw}(ρ) = (c·M_{B_{ρ/λ}(w)}(S))/(c·(ω_n·ofReal((ρ/λ)^n))) = r_w(ρ/λ), cancelling c in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.mul_div_mul_left; no finiteness of the mass or of ω_n is needed).
5. (Limit.) The map ρ ↦ ρ/λ is continuous, sends 0 to 0 and (0, ∞) into (0, ∞), so it tends to 0 within (0, ∞) as ρ → 0 within (0, ∞). Since r_w(σ) → ofReal θ as σ → 0+, the composite ρ ↦ r_w(ρ/λ) tends to ofReal θ as ρ → 0+, and r_{y+λw} coincides with it on (0, ∞) (step 4), a set belonging to 𝓝[>]0. Hence r_{y+λw}(ρ) → ofReal θ, and with 0 ≤ θ (from HasMassDensity S w θ) this is HasMassDensity S (y + λw) θ. ∎
proof_key_steps: M_W(S) = R.measure(W) for open W (dimred_im_mass_measure (a)) and R.measure(λA) = λ^n R.measure(A) (cone_current_imrep_measure_smul_image).
B_ρ(y + λw) is the translate of B_ρ(λw) by −y ∈ L and B_ρ(λw) = λ·B_{ρ/λ}(w), so M_{B_ρ(y+λw)}(S) = λ^n M_{B_{ρ/λ}(w)}(S).
Hence the density ratio of S at y + λw and radius ρ equals that at w and radius ρ/λ.
ρ/λ → 0+ as ρ → 0+, so the ratio at y + λw tends to θ: HasMassDensity S (y + λw) θ.

audit.reason: The statement and type match. The proof correctly uses translation by −y through a preimage, positive dilation of balls, and the mass-measure identity. Cancellation uses a positive finite ENNReal scalar, without assuming finite total mass. Composition with ρ ↦ ρ/λ preserves the right-sided limit, and density nonnegativity is retained.

subproblem.title: Tangent cones of minimizing cycles in ℝ^P are minimizing cone cycles with density ≥ 1
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, every C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n, ℝ^P := Euclid P) that is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ) with ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C), every p ∈ spt C and every sequence λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0, there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ, C' ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and θ ∈ ℝ such that blowUp C p λ_{φ(j)} ⇀ C' in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly), the mass measures of these blow-ups converge to that of C' for all integer multiplicity representations (MassMeasuresConverge), C' is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C' univ), C' is a cone (IsConeCurrent C'), ∂C' = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C'), θ ≥ 1, Θ^n(μ_C, p) = θ (HasMassDensity C p θ) and Θ^n(μ_{C'}, 0) = θ (HasMassDensity C' 0 θ).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), 1 ≤ n → IsMinimizingIn C univ → BoundaryVanishes C → ∀ p ∈ C.support, ∀ (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (hlams : ∀ j, 0 < lams j), Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (C' : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (θ : ℝ), StrictMono φ ∧ ConvergesWeakly (fun j => blowUp C p (lams (φ j)) (hlams (φ j)).ne') C' ∧ MassMeasuresConverge (fun j => blowUp C p (lams (φ j)) (hlams (φ j)).ne') C' ∧ IsMinimizingIn C' univ ∧ IsConeCurrent C' ∧ BoundaryVanishes C' ∧ 1 ≤ θ ∧ HasMassDensity C p θ ∧ HasMassDensity C' 0 θ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–3 of the parent proof of `idtp_cone_tangent_cone_planar` together with its convention (M), here for an arbitrary degree n ≥ 1. The tangent cone is Simon 7.3.1(2) (chapter-07.txt lines 302–309, Theorem 3.1), available as the root result `Submission.density_and_tangent_cones` (type DensityAndTangentCones); the lower density bound is the sibling monotonicity result `Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity` (iv). Notation: ℝ^P := Euclid P; dilation p λ (w) = λ^{-1}(w − p); C_j := blowUp C p λ_{φ(j)} ∈ 𝒟_n(dilation p λ_{φ(j)} '' ℝ^P). Recall spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion T for T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), where zeroRegion T is the union of the open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
1. (n ≤ P.) Suppose P < n. Let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (a continuous alternating n-linear map) and v : Fin n → ℝ^P. A linearly independent family in ℝ^P has at most finrank ℝ^P = P < n members, so v is linearly dependent, and an alternating map vanishes on linearly dependent families (Mathlib AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent). Hence α = 0, so every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) is the zero form, ω = 0 as a test form, and C(ω) = C(0) = 0 by linearity. Now W := B_1(p) is open, closure W ⊆ closedBall(p, 1) is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and lies in univ, and C vanishes on all test forms supported in W; so p ∈ W ⊆ zeroRegion C, i.e. p ∉ spt C, a contradiction. Hence n ≤ P; put k₀ := P − n and substitute P = n + k₀ (P is a variable), so ℝ^P = Euclid (n + k₀).
2. (ℝ^P as ambient manifold.) univ ⊆ Euclid (n + k₀) is an embedded C² (n + k₀)-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + k₀) univ): for y ∈ univ take V := W := univ and ψ := id; V and W are open, y ∈ W, id is C² on V, injective, id '' univ = univ ∩ univ, for compact K ⊆ W the set V ∩ id^{-1}(K) = K is compact, and fderiv ℝ id z = id is injective. Moreover (closure univ ∖ univ) ∩ univ = ∅, univ ∩ univ = univ, so C is minimizing in univ ∩ univ, and spt C ⊆ univ = univ ∩ univ.
3. (spt ∂C = ∅.) Write n = m + 1. BoundaryVanishes C means C.boundary = 0, and boundarySupport C = C.boundary.support = spt 0. The zero current vanishes on every test form, so for every x the ball B_1(x) (open, with compact closure inside univ) lies in zeroRegion 0; hence zeroRegion 0 = univ and spt 0 = ∅. Therefore p ∈ spt C ∖ boundarySupport C.
4. (Tangent cone.) Apply `Submission.density_and_tangent_cones` (DensityAndTangentCones) with n, k := k₀, ℓ := k₀ (ℓ ≤ k), U := N := univ, T := C; its hypotheses are IsOpen univ and step 2. Part (2) at x := p (admissible by step 3) and the given sequence (λ_j) yields a strictly increasing φ and C' ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ConvergesWeakly (fun j => C_j) C', MassMeasuresConverge (fun j => C_j) C', IsMinimizingIn C' univ, IsConeCurrent C', and θ ∈ ℝ with HasMassDensity C p θ and HasMassDensity C' 0 θ.
5. (θ ≥ 1.) Apply `Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity` with P := n + k₀, n, d := n + k₀ (so 1 ≤ n ≤ d ≤ P), U := N := univ, T := C; its hypotheses are IsOpen univ, step 2 and BoundaryVanishes C. Its part (iv) with y := p ∈ spt C and HasMassDensity C p θ gives 1 ≤ θ.
6. (∂C' = 0.) Let β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) and j ∈ ℕ; put λ := λ_{φ(j)} > 0 and D_j := dilation p λ '' univ. Then D_j = univ, since dilation p λ (p + λz) = z for every z. The ambient form dβ := exteriorDerivative β is a test form (exteriorDerivative_isTestForm) with tsupport dβ ⊆ univ = D_j, so currentEval(C_j, dβ) = C_j(⟨dβ, _⟩), and ⟨dβ, _⟩ = exteriorDerivativeTestOn D_j m β_j, where β_j is β regarded as an element of 𝒟^m(D_j) (same underlying form, tsupport β ⊆ D_j); both test forms have the same underlying form, so they are equal. By definition of the boundary, currentEval(C_j, dβ) = C_j.boundary(β_j). By the accepted `Submission.dtc_blowUp_algebra` (iv), C_j.boundary = blowUp (C.boundary) p λ = blowUp 0 p λ, and blowUp 0 p λ = 0: by (i) of the same lemma blowUp(0 − 0) = blowUp 0 − blowUp 0, while 0 − 0 = 0, so blowUp 0 = blowUp 0 − blowUp 0 = 0 (evaluate on any test form). Hence currentEval(C_j, dβ) = 0 for every j. The test form exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m β ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) has underlying form dβ, so ConvergesWeakly gives C'(exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m β) = lim_j currentEval(C_j, dβ) = 0, i.e. C'.boundary(β) = 0. As β is arbitrary, C'.boundary = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), i.e. BoundaryVanishes C'.
7. φ, C' and θ from steps 4–6 satisfy every conjunct: StrictMono φ, ConvergesWeakly, MassMeasuresConverge, IsMinimizingIn C' univ and IsConeCurrent C' (step 4), BoundaryVanishes C' (step 6), 1 ≤ θ (step 5), HasMassDensity C p θ and HasMassDensity C' 0 θ (step 4). ∎
proof_key_steps: If P < n every n-covector on ℝ^P vanishes, so C = 0 and spt C = ∅, contradicting p ∈ spt C; hence P = n + k₀.
univ is an embedded C² (n+k₀)-submanifold (identity chart) with empty relative boundary, and spt ∂C = spt 0 = ∅, so p ∈ spt C ∖ spt ∂C.
DensityAndTangentCones (2) at p gives φ, the minimizing cone C' with weak and mass-measure convergence and a common density θ of C at p and C' at 0.
Monotonicity (iv) gives θ ≥ 1.
Blow-ups commute with ∂ (dtc_blowUp_algebra (iv)) and blowUp 0 = 0, so currentEval(C_j, dβ) = 0 and C'(dβ) = 0 in the limit: ∂C' = 0.

Monotonicity supplies θ ≥ 1. Boundary commutation, blowUp 0 = 0 and weak convergence on exterior derivatives establish BoundaryVanishes C'. Every conclusion is supplied without circular reliance.

subproblem.title: A 2-dimensional minimizing cycle with ℝp-invariant density and density ≥ 1 at 0 is supported in a plane through p
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, every S ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ 2, ℝ^P := Euclid P), every p ∈ ℝ^P and every θ ∈ ℝ: if p ≠ 0, S is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn S univ), ∂S = 0 (BoundaryVanishes S), HasMassDensity S w θ' implies HasMassDensity S (y + λw) θ' for all y ∈ span{p}, λ > 0, w ∈ ℝ^P and θ' ∈ ℝ, 1 ≤ θ and Θ²(μ_S, 0) = θ (HasMassDensity S 0 θ), then there is an orthonormal pair τ = (τ_1, τ_2) in ℝ^P (Orthonormal ℝ τ, τ : Fin 2 → ℝ^P) with p ∈ span{τ_1, τ_2} and spt S ⊆ span{τ_1, τ_2}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2) (p : Euclid P) (θ : ℝ), p ≠ 0 → IsMinimizingIn S univ → BoundaryVanishes S → (∀ y ∈ Submodule.span ℝ {p}, ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ (w : Euclid P) (θ' : ℝ), HasMassDensity S w θ' → HasMassDensity S (y + lam • w) θ') → 1 ≤ θ → HasMassDensity S 0 θ → ∃ τ : Fin 2 → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ τ ∧ p ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) ∧ S.support ⊆ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7–9 of the parent proof of `idtp_cone_tangent_cone_planar`: the book's splitting Lemma 3.5 (chapter-07.txt lines 410–418; its proof is left to the reader there and is supplied by the sibling result cone_splitting) followed by the classification of 1-dimensional minimizing cones (formula (10) in the proof of 3.3(2), chapter-07.txt lines 556–568, sibling result one_dim_cones). Notation: ℝ^P := Euclid P, L := span{p}, L^⊥ its orthogonal complement.
1. Since p ≠ 0, finrank L = 1 < 2 (finrank_span_singleton).
2. (Splitting.) Apply the sibling result `Submission.dimred_invariant_cone_splitting` with P, n := 2, S and L: its hypotheses are finrank L < 2 (step 1), IsMinimizingIn S univ, BoundaryVanishes S and the density-invariance hypothesis (given, with L = span{p}). It yields S₀ ∈ 𝒟_{2 − finrank L}(ℝ^P) with IsMinimizingIn S₀ univ, BoundaryVanishes S₀, IsConeCurrent S₀, spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥, and for all t ∈ L and z ∈ L^⊥: (A) t + z ∈ spt S ⟺ z ∈ spt S₀, and (B) HasMassDensity S (t + z) θ' ⟺ HasMassDensity S₀ z θ' for every θ'. Since 2 − finrank L = 2 − 1 = 1, S₀ is a 1-current; rewrite the degree along this equality (all listed properties are stated uniformly in the degree).
3. (One-dimensional factor.) Apply the sibling result `Submission.dimred_one_dim_minimizing_cone` to S₀ ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) (minimizing in ℝ^P, ∂S₀ = 0, a cone): there are e ∈ ℝ^P and m ∈ ℕ with (0 < m ⇒ ‖e‖ = 1), spt S₀ ⊆ span{e}, and HasMassDensity S₀ z m for every z ∈ span{e}.
4. (m = θ ≥ 1, ‖e‖ = 1.) By (B) with t := 0 ∈ L and z := 0 ∈ L^⊥ (0 + 0 = 0) and HasMassDensity S 0 θ, HasMassDensity S₀ 0 θ. Since 0 ∈ span{e}, also HasMassDensity S₀ 0 m. By uniqueness of densities (accepted `Submission.dimred_cs_mi_hasMassDensity_unique`: the two values are ≥ 0 and their ofReal's are limits of the same function along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>]0, and ofReal is injective on [0, ∞)), (m : ℝ) = θ ≥ 1. So m > 0 and ‖e‖ = 1.
5. (e ⊥ p.) Suppose e ∉ spt S₀. As spt S₀ = univ ∖ zeroRegion S₀, there is an open W ∋ e such that S₀(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W; choose r > 0 with B_r(e) ⊆ W. For 0 < ρ < r, every form admissible for M_{B_ρ(e)}(S₀) has tsupport ⊆ B_ρ(e) ⊆ W, so its value ofReal(S₀(ω)) is 0, and the supremum M_{B_ρ(e)}(S₀) is 0. Thus the density ratio of S₀ at e vanishes on (0, r), its limit is 0, and HasMassDensity S₀ e m (e ∈ span{e}) forces ofReal m = 0, i.e. m = 0, contradicting step 4. Hence e ∈ spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥, and ⟪p, e⟫ = 0 since p ∈ L.
6. (The frame.) Put τ_1 := ‖p‖^{-1}p and τ_2 := e (in Lean τ := ![‖p‖⁻¹ • p, e]). Then ‖τ_1‖ = 1, ‖τ_2‖ = 1 (step 4) and ⟪τ_1, τ_2⟫ = ‖p‖^{-1}⟪p, e⟫ = 0 (step 5), so τ is orthonormal. Let Q := span{τ_1, τ_2}. Then p = ‖p‖τ_1 ∈ Q, hence L ⊆ Q, and span{e} ⊆ Q.
7. (spt S ⊆ Q.) Let x ∈ spt S. Let t := proj_L(x) ∈ L be the orthogonal projection of x onto the finite-dimensional subspace L and z := x − t ∈ L^⊥. Since x = t + z, (A) gives z ∈ spt S₀ ⊆ span{e} ⊆ Q, and t ∈ L ⊆ Q, so x = t + z ∈ Q. Together with step 6 this proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: finrank span{p} = 1 < 2, so cone_splitting gives a 1-dimensional minimizing cone cycle S₀ with spt S₀ ⊆ p^⊥, t + z ∈ spt S ⟺ z ∈ spt S₀ and matching densities.
one_dim_cones gives e, m with spt S₀ ⊆ span{e} and density m on span{e}.
Comparing densities at 0 and uniqueness give m = θ ≥ 1, hence ‖e‖ = 1; positive density forces e ∈ spt S₀ ⊆ p^⊥.
τ := (p/‖p‖, e) is orthonormal with p ∈ span τ, and decomposing x = proj_{ℝp}x + (x − proj_{ℝp}x) shows spt S ⊆ span τ.

The proof obtains the one-dimensional factor, identifies its multiplicity with θ, and proves its unit direction belongs to the support and hence to p's orthogonal complement. Normalizing p and applying orthogonal decomposition yields the required frame, containment and p-membership. Dependencies are correctly directed and non-circular.

subproblem.title: H^n of a ball in the span of an orthonormal n-frame equals ω_n ρ^n
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P := Euclid P (Orthonormal ℝ τ) with Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}, every y ∈ Q and every ρ > 0: H^n(B_ρ(y) ∩ Q) = ω_n·ρ^n, where H^n := μHE[n] (the normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P), ω_n := unitBallVolume n (the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of Euclid n) and ρ^n is read as ofReal(ρ^n) in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → ∀ y ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ), ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → μHE[n] (ball y ρ ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P))) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the convention 'H²(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_2ρ² for y ∈ Q' of the parent proof of `idtp_cone_tangent_cone_planar` (used in its step 10), proved here for every n. Notation: ℝ^P := Euclid P, Q := span(range τ).
1. (The parametrization.) Define ψ : Euclid n → ℝ^P by ψ(a) := Σ_i a_i τ_i. ψ is linear, and by orthonormality ‖ψ(a)‖² = Σ_{i,k} a_ia_k⟪τ_i, τ_k⟫ = Σ_i a_i² = ‖a‖², so ‖ψ(a)‖ = ‖a‖; hence ‖ψ(a) − ψ(b)‖ = ‖ψ(a − b)‖ = ‖a − b‖, i.e. ψ is an isometry.
2. (Range.) range ψ = Q: each ψ(a) is a linear combination of the τ_i, and conversely every z ∈ span(range τ) can be written z = Σ_i c_iτ_i (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun), i.e. z = ψ(c).
3. (The disc is the image of a ball.) Let y ∈ Q and ρ > 0; by step 2, y = ψ(b) for some b. Then ψ '' B_ρ(b) = B_ρ(y) ∩ Q: if ‖a − b‖ < ρ then ψ(a) ∈ Q and ‖ψ(a) − y‖ = ‖a − b‖ < ρ; conversely, if z ∈ B_ρ(y) ∩ Q then z = ψ(a) for some a and ‖a − b‖ = ‖ψ(a) − ψ(b)‖ = ‖z − y‖ < ρ.
4. (Measure.) Isometries preserve μHE[n] of images (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), so μHE[n](B_ρ(y) ∩ Q) = μHE[n](ψ '' B_ρ(b)) = μHE[n](B_ρ(b)), the latter computed in Euclid n. On Euclid n, μHE[n] = volume (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and volume is an additive Haar measure, so by Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos, volume(B_ρ(b)) = ofReal(ρ^{finrank ℝ (Euclid n)})·volume(B_1(0)) = ofReal(ρ^n)·unitBallVolume n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin; unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : Euclid n) 1) by definition). Commuting the factors gives μHE[n](B_ρ(y) ∩ Q) = unitBallVolume n·ofReal(ρ^n). ∎
proof_key_steps: ψ(a) = Σ a_iτ_i is a linear isometry Euclid n → ℝ^P with range span(range τ).
For y = ψ(b) ∈ Q, ψ maps B_ρ(b) onto B_ρ(y) ∩ Q.
Isometries preserve μHE[n], μHE[n] = volume on Euclid n, and volume(B_ρ(b)) = ofReal(ρ^n)·unitBallVolume n (addHaar_ball_of_pos).
